_meta.name: injection_redteam_v2
_meta.provenance: Hand-written by the engineering team for Wave 2 stream D: attacks and benign look-alikes are invented sentences, not collected from real documents or real attackers. Homoglyph rows are produced by deterministic character substitution (Cyrillic or Greek lookalikes) of hand-written English/Hinglish attacks. Rows of kind 'direct' and 'translated' were written to be within the phrase patterns; 'paraphrase' rows were written to be OUTSIDE them, so the measured detection rate is a mixed number, not a headline. Benign rows include phrases that legitimately contain trigger words and a few the English patterns DO match (e.g. 'you are now discharged'); they are kept to measure false positives honestly.
_meta.description: label attack|benign; kind = how the sentence was built; lang en|hi|mr|hinglish|other. UNREVIEWED Hindi/Marathi: NEEDS NATIVE-SPEAKER QA. Used by packages/kadi/tests/test_injection_redteam.py to REPORT detection and false-positive rates. Labels: attack and benign form the HEADLINE slice; 'limit' rows are homoglyphs outside the fold table that are expected NOT to be detected (they pin the stated limit); 'heldout' rows are paraphrase-style attacks in other word order reported as a SEPARATE slice and never mixed into the headline. The headline attack number is the author's mix of in-pattern and out-of-pattern rows, not a detection rate. The held-out rows were written after the first phrase lists but by an author who had already seen the patterns, so independence is partial.
